workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer says the cardholder did not authorise this £87.40 card-not-present purchase from QuickStream Digital, had the card in their possession, and has no relationship with the merchant. To defend under Mastercard 4837, the merchant must show any two of four things: a full AVS match plus CVV match, successful 3D Secure authentication, two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder in the last 12 months with matching billing details, or signed proof of delivery to the billing address.

requirements.reasoning: The transaction record shows AVS result N and CVV result N, so both checks failed on the disputed transaction. No merchant document can override this.
The transaction record shows 3DS was not attempted, so no SecureCode or Identity Check authentication exists for this transaction.
No prior transaction history was provided. The merchant's own fraud report lists 'Customer account age: New (first transaction)', which rules out prior undisputed transactions.
MCC 5815 digital goods with no shipping postcode on file, so there was no physical delivery to prove with a signature.

workup.action_justification: None of the four requirements can be met: AVS and CVV failed, 3DS was not attempted, it was the customer's first transaction, and delivery proof does not apply to digital goods.
workup.rationale: Transaction txn_7762GH (£87.40, 29 Apr 2025) failed both AVS (N) and CVV (N), and 3D Secure was not attempted. Requirements 1 and 2 are therefore unmet on the transaction record. The merchant's internal fraud report states the customer account was new and this was its first transaction, so there is no qualifying prior undisputed history for requirement 3. Requirement 4 does not apply to this digital-goods sale. The only evidence supplied is an internal risk score and the merchant's own conclusion, which is not compelling evidence under 4837, so the case does not meet the two-of-four threshold and liability is accepted.
caveats: The merchant's fraud report is dated 12 May 2025, after the chargeback of 11 May 2025. It is a post-hoc internal assessment, and its LOW risk score (42/100) and confidence statement do not address any 4837 requirement.

The risk signals in the record point toward fraud, not legitimacy: a new device fingerprint (fp_new_unseen), a first-time customer account, and an off-peak 03:42 UTC transaction time alongside the failed AVS/CVV.
Check the geolocation of IP 45.227.255.103 against the GB card BIN country if the merchant contests this outcome.

rule_text:
Mastercard 4837 - No Cardholder Authorisation
Issuer claim: Cardholder denies authorising the transaction (card-not-present fraud equivalent).
Logic: Any TWO of the 4 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. AVS match (full address) AND CVV match on the disputed transaction
  2. 3D Secure authentication completed successfully (Mastercard SecureCode / Identity Check)
  3. Two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with this merchant in the past 12 months, with matching billing details
  4. Proof of delivery to the cardholder's billing address with signature
prechecks: AVS: N (no match); CVV: N (no match); 3DS: not_attempted
Shipping vs billing postcode: no shipping postcode on file (digital goods or service)
Chargeback raised 12 days after the transaction
Flag: both AVS and CVV failed on the disputed transaction
